title: Add queryable token-cost index and prompt-shape adaptive alerting
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a compact, queryable token-cost index for fast per-tenant cost drilldowns and a new prompt-shape-aware alert weighting component. Includes dashboard and alert rule updates.
description:
Context and motivation: Production cost investigations are often expensive because token-level cost attribution requires full trace hydration or heavy aggregation jobs. This PR introduces a compact, queryable token-cost index (token_cost_idx) that stores per-invocation token-cost signatures and a lightweight prompt-shape fingerprint. The goal is to enable sub-second drilldowns for common SRE workflows and to reduce noise in SLO alerts by weighting incidents against historical prompt-shape cohorts.

What this PR changes (single string):
- Introduces a new invocation digest proto (compact fields: invocation_id, tenant_id, model, token_cost_sum, token_phase_histogram, prompt_shape_hash, timestamp) and a migration to generate these digests in the ingestion pipeline.
- Adds an indexed storage path and a small query service (token-cost-indexer) that supports queries like: top tenants by token-cost in time window, examples of invocations matching a prompt-shape hash, and aggregated per-phase cost breakdown.
- Adds a PromptShapeAlertWeighting component used by alert-router: alerts are scored against the recent centroid of prompt-shape cohorts for the route and alerts below a similarity threshold are deprioritized.
- Dashboard additions: compact "Token Cost Index Explorer" Grafana panel (fast lookup UI), new per-route prompt-shape cohort sparkline.
- Alerting: updates to default SLO alerting rules to expose a new "prompt_shape_similarity" label and use adaptive thresholds for routes with high prompt-shape churn.
- Tests: end-to-end test for index ingestion, unit tests for digest serialization and similarity scoring, and a small load test proving query latency under synthetic workload.

Relevant notes on implementation details:
- The invocation digest is intentionally compact to bound storage growth: token_phase_histogram is 4-slab histogram (input, generation-start, kv-cache-miss, generation-end) and prompt_shape_hash is a 64-bit locality-preserving hash of token position distribution + delimiter counts.
- Index storage uses existing sstable-backed append-only shards under telemetry/indexer, permitting cheap range scans by time and tenant. The query API supports a small set of pre-aggregations to avoid heavy joins in the UI.
- Similarity scoring uses cosine on 16-d embeddings derived from the prompt_shape_hash with a cache of recent centroids per-route; this keeps per-alert compute small (O(centroid_size)).

CI summary:
- Initial run: failed (integration test flake in tests/load_indexer_test.go due to race on shard cleanup).
- Fix: added mutex and added deterministic cleanup ordering in commit e5e63c1.
- Final run: all checks passed (unit, integration, lints, go vet).

Why this is different from prior work: Existing observability changes have focused mainly on token rollups, span sampling, and coarse attribution. This PR adds a lightweight, queryable first-class index for token-cost signatures with prompt-shape-aware alert weighting. The index is intended for operational workflows (on-call, RCA) rather than high-volume billing exports — a complementary fast-path to heavy analytics jobs.

Backward compatibility and migration: The ingestion path emits digests in addition to the existing telemetry streams, so no consumers are broken. There is a one-time migration job (scripts/telemetry/reindex_token_cost_index.sh) that can backfill from raw traces; the migration is optional for customers who do not need historical lookups.

Operational considerations & rollout plan:
- Roll out indexer to canary cluster with shard_count=8 for 48 hours, validate query P95 < 400ms under 1000 qps synthetic load.
- Enable prompt-shape weighting behind feature flag (observability.prompt_shape_weighting) and ramp from 0% to 100% over two weeks for routes with >10k invocations/day.
- Add retention TTL configuration, default 30 days, adjustable per-tenant via enterprise settings.

Merge outcome: Squash merge to main. Merge commit: 9f3c7b2.

Playbook snippets (copied into docs/observability/playbooks/token_cost_index.md): example query strings, example alert de-escalation command, and how to reindex a tenant.

If you want to try it locally: see telemetry/indexer/README.md — includes docker-compose for a single-shard mode and sample curl queries.
